name: Inoue Seikichi Shoten
about: Inoue Seikichi Shoten was founded in 1868 in Shirasawa, a former post town on the old Oshu Kaido road that is now part of Utsunomiya, Tochigi. Its sake is sold as Sawahime.

Since the 2004 brewing season every bottle, from everyday sake to competition daiginjo, has been made from rice grown in Tochigi. The brewery calls this its Shin Jizake Sengen, a commitment to local rice, local water and the local climate. Hiroshi Inoue has led it since 2013.
Sawahime was named Champion Sake at the International Wine Challenge in 2010 and again in 2022, and joined the IWC Sake Hall of Fame in 2026.
